model_interpretation.claim: A scalar eight-way unroll may expose more independent minimum/index chains than the previously measured two-, three-, and four-accumulator candidates, reducing loop-carried dependence on random and decreasing inputs. The lower measured aggregate time for two accumulators (2.2604 µs) than for three (3.0152 µs) or four (2.8135 µs) shows that more chains are not automatically better; eight also raises initialization, fold, and instruction-pressure costs, so correctness and per-pattern measurements are needed to assess the tradeoff.

items.subject: Unrolled scalar argmin with independent accumulators
items.objective: Explore a compiler-friendly scalar scan with a small fixed unroll factor and several independent (minimum value, earliest index) accumulators. Fold the accumulators with signed-value then lowest-index ordering; handle any remainder scalarly. Do not use explicit SIMD or parallel workers in this branch. Measure whether reduced loop-carried dependence helps on both random and decreasing inputs, after correctness checks.
